newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul seek custody of US soldier accused of murder.
newsitem.headline: Seoul seek custody of US soldier accused of murder.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors will ask the U.S. military to hand over a U.S. soldier alleged to have admitted to murdering a South Korean woman in September, local media reported on Thursday.
Seoul District Court issued an arrest warrant on Thursday for Private Eric Munnich, from Chicago, on charges of killing Lee Ki-sun, state television said.
Prosecution officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
In early September the body of Lee, 44, was found in a boarding house near a U.S. military base north of Seoul where Munnich is stationed.
The prosecution plans to ask the U.S. Army to transfer Munnich to the custody of local judicial authorities, the domestic Yonhap news agency said.
The U.S. military said Munnich, now detained at a U.S. military installation, has admitted to the murder during joint questioning by South Korean police and U.S. military investigators.
The commander of U.S. military forces in South Korea General John Tillely has described the murder as "tragic and nonsensical".
The United States maintains 37,000 troops in South Korea. The country technically remains at war with North Korea after the 1950-53 Korean War ended with a ceasefire rather than a peace pact.
